quarterly_data.quarter: TeraWulf press release: Kentucky PSC Approves 482 MW Power Agreement for TeraWulf's (08-24-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: In its August 21, 2026 order the Kentucky Public Service Commission approved the Retail Electric Service Agreement (RESA) supporting up to 482 MW of electric service for TeraWulf's Justified Data Campus in Hancock County, Kentucky (the former Century Aluminum Hawesville facility, where approximately 482 MW of existing transmission capability remains available), authorizing Big Rivers Electric Corporation and Kenergy Corp. to implement it. TeraWulf bears the market, transmission, delivery and customer-specific infrastructure costs of its load, with substantial credit-support obligations. Based on current expected development costs of approximately $10 million to $12 million per MW of critical IT load, TeraWulf estimates approximately $4.0 billion to $4.5 billion of investment in site development and the initial data halls, excluding customers' investment in computing equipment. CEO Paul Prager: 'Power is the gating factor for AI infrastructure, but how you bring that power to market matters.'
quarterly_data.figure: up to 482 MW of electric service approved; approximately $10 million to $12 million per MW of critical IT load; approximately $4.0 billion to $4.5 billion of investment in site development and initial data halls
